David — thanks, useful starter. Answers below:
- Typical request (prompt+response): ~1,400 tokens average for long-form summarization jobs; shorter assistant queries ~300 tokens. For POC expect 60/40 long-form/short.
- Concurrency: baseline 6 heavy concurrent jobs (long-form) and ~40 short assistant calls concurrent during business hours; peak concurrency observed in stress tests hit ~60 active requests.
- We target p95 around 600ms for user-facing flows (acceptable up to 1s for async long-form jobs). p99 should be under 2.5s.
- Burst profile: we see short storms when pipeline backfills complete — typical spike: 90–120 seconds, up to 20x baseline for those 90–120s, roughly twice a day during batch windows. Also rare events where traffic jumps ~100x for ~30s.

Procurement (procure@heliotrope.ai) is on cc — they want to know the minimum pilot commit, and any early termination flexibility.

—Sanjay

Sanjay — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. High-level proposal for a 3-month pilot:
- Pilot commit: 2 "slabs" (each slab = 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs with dedicated networking), enough for steady state + 1.5x headroom.
- Autoscale/burst pool: attach a burst pool (elastic) sized to add up to 6 slabs on demand for short storms; autoscale driven by queue depth and token rate.
- Latency fit: aim to serve short assistant calls on a quantized 7B variant (expected p95 < 250ms). Long-form summarization routes to a 13B model on A10G slab with 600ms p95 expectation per your target.
- Fallbacks: add smaller-ops model-variant for TTL-sensitive endpoints to keep latency guarantees during extreme events.

Cost/ops note: pilot 2 slabs + burst entitlement lets us demonstrate SLOs during daily 2x–20x bursts without a large commit. We’ll include explicit warm-up and pre-warm routines in the runbook so cold KV cache doesn't kill p95.

Attaching a short draft proposal (heliotrope_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf) with the slab math and an outline for an ops-runbook. Priyom — can you validate tokens/sec per GPU numbers and a recommended safety multiplier?

—Kim

Hi all — I ran the numbers off Sanjay's traffic profile and our current kernel stack assumptions. Summary below (rounded for clarity):

Assumptions:
- Model split: short assistant -> 7B quantized variant; long-form -> 13B un-quantized (or lightly quantized)
- Typical sequence length: short 300 tokens, long 1,400 tokens
- Target p95: 600ms for long-form; sub-300ms for short assistant on quantized stack

Measured baseline throughput (per GPU, steady-state token generation, beam=1):
- A10G-equivalent (our standard slab GPU): ~220 tokens/sec for 13B long-form (p95 ~450–650ms depending on length and KV hit rate)
- A10G-equivalent on 7B quantized: ~850 tokens/sec (p95 < 250ms)
- T4-equivalent: ~80 tokens/sec (not recommended for long-form p95 targets)

Mapping to slabs and headroom:
- Pilot slab definition: 4 x A10G-equivalent GPUs (networked, shared KV cache). One slab sustained token capacity (13B) ~ 880 tokens/sec. With 1.5x ops headroom that's ~1,320 tokens/sec.
- Sanjay baseline calculation: (6 long-form * 1,400 tokens / avg request duration) approximate sustained baseline tokens/sec: long-form concurrency converts to ~1,400 tokens/min per job -> ~23 tokens/sec per job * 6 = ~138 tokens/sec. Short assistant adds ~40 sessions * 5 tokens/sec ~200 tokens/sec. Baseline ~= 340 tokens/sec.
- Burst: your observed short storms (20x baseline) -> up to ~6,800 tokens/sec during 90–120s surges. Rare micro-spikes (100x) -> ~34,000 tokens/sec for ~30s.

Recommendation:
- Start pilot with 2 slabs (2 * 880 = 1,760 tokens/sec nominal on 13B traffic) which comfortably covers baseline (340 tps) with 5x headroom for short bursts and 2x for 90–120s storms when combined with autoscale.
- Configure burst autoscale pool to add up to 6 additional slabs (quick-turn up to add ~5,280 tokens/sec per slab set) to absorb 20x storms; autoscale warm-up using pre-warm routine (cache priming) to reduce p95 ramp.
- Safety multipliers: plan for 1.5x sustained headroom and 4–8x short-burst entitlement depending on contract tolerance. For billing, show committed slabs + burst entitlement credits.

Ops notes:
- Cache priming: run a background KV prefix warm during known batch windows to avoid cold p95 spikes.
- Canary scaling: roll autoscale in thresholds with a canary slab before full-scale-up.

I can drop the exact per-GPU measurements and a sensitivity table into the HubSpot deal doc if that helps procurement.

—Priyom
